title: Juniper and the Inventory
premise: Odile Fairweather, a translator whose childhood language is dissolving word by word into borrowed ones, learns that the house where he grew up—abandoned since his mother's death—is being auctioned to settle debts he never knew existed. Returning for the sale, he confronts the estranged half-sister who kept the house alive and the neighbor who witnessed the silence that broke their family. As the auction nears, Odile realizes his lifelong strategy of invisibility has cost him every goodbye he owed; the novel ends with him standing in the empty parlor on closing day, speaking his farewell aloud in a language only three people still remember—one of them himself.
about_author: Felix Ravensworth is the pen name of a former court interpreter who spent fifteen years translating other people's confessions before writing any of his own. He lives in a coastal town where the old language survives mainly in place names and arguments.

chapters.title: The Inventory of Unsaid Things
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In the city, Odile translates a deposition and loses another childhood word mid-sentence, then receives notice of the auction. He begins a literal inventory of everything left unsaid—to his dead mother, to the sister who stopped writing. The beat is quiet dread: the past arriving as paperwork.

chapters.title: What the House Kept
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, shifting to second person in memory passages. He returns to the town, walks the house, and meets Maren, the half-sister who paid its taxes alone for years. Their first conversation is all subtext and borrowed words. The beat is guilt surfacing: the house remembers what he chose to forget.

chapters.title: Auction Day
chapters.summary: Odile's POV with interludes from Maren's letters read aloud. At the auction, the neighbor Halvard reveals why Odile's mother went silent—a debt taken on to protect him—and bidding turns bitter between developers and townspeople. Odile freezes when called to speak. The beat is public exposure: invisibility fails exactly when it matters.

chapters.title: Closing
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. On the final closing day, before the new owners take possession, Odile and Maren walk the empty rooms together. In the parlor he speaks his inventory aloud—the apologies, the goodbyes—in the fading language, and Maren answers in kind. The beat is release: justice outside any law, rendered simply by saying it out loud.
